title: I Used the Gem-Tumbler Hours on the Chair Who Camped the Barrel

parts.text: I opened tumbler four at 2:04 p.m. and chair Nessa was already running grit in our numbered barrel. The card said: ONE BARREL. SEVEN DAYS. GRIT STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was forty-five, club member, holding a grit chart that listed our stage. Nessa shrugged. "Chairs are the grit." I photographed the card, the booking, and her stones in our barrel. Then I asked for the tumbler log. At 2:12 the shop pinged why Nessa's name was on our week. I kept my voice shop-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop can see Nessa's stones in our barrel during our week.

social.video_title: She ran grit in our numbered barrel on our week — Part 1/2
social.description: Gem tumbler, a chair in our barrel, a seven-day clock she posted. I logged the grit. Would you have asked for the tumbler log?

parts.text: Nessa called it a polish until the shop asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the stones still. The barrel went back to our lid. Nessa ran her own seven and told the next chair atmosphere was always about shine. Shine is a word chairs use when a booking exists. Tumbler policy now has a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE GRIT. I keep our barrel on a labeled shelf. Nessa brown-bags her jokes. The shop finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Tumbler log, numbered barrel, and a second line on the card. Was a polish ever our week?
